body:
Developer Cold Iron Studios shuts down cloud version of $60 game with no refunds

In a significant move that has left many gamers frustrated, Cold Iron Studios has announced the shutdown of the cloud version of its $60 game, “Aliens: Fireteam Elite,” on the Nintendo Switch. This decision has sparked discussions about digital ownership and the implications of cloud gaming, especially when players lose access to purchased content without the option for refunds.

What happened

Cold Iron Studios, the developer behind “Aliens: Fireteam Elite,” recently informed players that the cloud-based version of the game on the Nintendo Switch would be discontinued. This announcement means that players who purchased the game will no longer have access to it, as the game relies on cloud servers to function. The shutdown has raised concerns among the gaming community, particularly regarding the lack of refunds for those who invested in the game. Players are left with no recourse to recover their financial investment, as the game will simply become unplayable after the service ends.

Why it matters

The closure of the cloud version of “Aliens: Fireteam Elite” serves as a stark reminder of the vulnerabilities associated with digital ownership. Unlike physical copies of games, which players can keep and play indefinitely, cloud-based games are subject to the whims of the developers and service providers. This situation highlights a growing concern in the gaming industry about the long-term viability of digital purchases and the rights of consumers. As more games move to cloud-based platforms, players may find themselves at risk of losing access to their purchases without any compensation or alternative options. This incident could lead to increased scrutiny of cloud gaming models and prompt discussions about consumer protections in the digital marketplace.

Source: Ars Technica.
